newsitem.title: LATVIA: O/N RATES STABLE, DEMAND FOR LATS SEEN RISING.
newsitem.headline: O/N RATES STABLE, DEMAND FOR LATS SEEN RISING.

text.p: Latvian overnight rates were stable on Tuesday and demand for lats remained strong ahead of Friday's deadline for Russia's Gazprom to pay for its stake in Latvian Gas.
Overnight rates were steady at a bid/ask of 3.0/4.0 percent and dealers did not expect any sigificant changes this week as the liquidity situation in the banking sector had stabilised.
The lat gained slightly against the dollar and was trading at 0.5856/61 on the interbank market, near the central bank intervention rate of 0.5853.

Dealers said that demand for lats was strong and was expected to stay that way for the rest of the week ahead of Friday's shareholders' meeting of Latvian Gas. Russia's Gazprom must pay for its stake by then, dealers said.
Wednesday's auction of 12 million lats worth of Latvian T-bills was also expected to increase the demand for lats.
But it was not expected to influence the overnight market as dealers expected foreign investors to snap up the lion's share of the T-bills.
